text:
Sam (eng-platform): Heads-up — baking a proposal for handling sensitive fields in telemetry before we flip the new OTLP routing rules on Friday. Two options: encrypt fields inline in SDK/exporter, or redact at the collector/sidecar. Wanted quick feedback on tradeoffs.

Maya (eng-runtime): +1 to discuss. main concerns: latency and key access from SDKs.

Priya (eng-security): If we encrypt in the SDK/exporter, we need a key-per-tenant or envelope key pattern, and we must ensure keys are never exfiltrated. That reduces server-side visibility for debug.

Tomas (infra): Collector-side redaction keeps keys central, but then we still ingest plaintext into our network which triggers compliance flags for some customers. Also harder to prove we never stored it.

Kira (compliance): For regulated customers we must show an audit trail of who could decrypt and when. Collector redaction helps because we never persist the sensitive value in object storage, but ingestion still touches it. Encryption at source avoids that but adds key distribution/audit complexity.

Sam (eng-platform): High-level trade-offs I sketched: 
- SDK/exporter encryption: earliest protection, still searchable only if we add tokenization/hashed buckets, needs client key material or a KMS call from SDK.
- Collector redaction: simpler keys, central audit, easy to roll out policy changes, but requires network gating/ingest approvals for PII customers.

Priya (eng-security): Also think about SLOs. Calling KMS from each SDK event will inflate tail latency. Could mitigate with local envelope key cached by SDK rotated by backend. But that introduces trust and rotation complexity.

Maya (eng-runtime): What about hybrid: SDK marks fields as "sensitive": true and either redacts or encrypts depending on route? Example: internal prod -> encrypt at SDK; hosted customers -> collector redaction. We already have routing policies in the API layer.

Sam (eng-platform): sketch of config we might use (collector side pseudocode):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols: [grpc, http]
processors:
  redact:
    fields: [attributes.user.email, attributes.request.body.ssn]
    strategy: remove # or replace: "[REDACTED]"
exporters:
  otlp/secure_sink:
    endpoint: "https://sensitive-archive.redwood-internal"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [redact, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/secure_sink]
```

Tomas (infra): For the SDK-encrypt approach we'd need a compatible exporter change. Example header pattern: `X-Redwood-Encrypted: v1` and values base64(envelope). Then collector would skip decryption except for a gated audit path.

Kira (compliance): Also flag: retention windows differ. Audit logs for decrypt ops must be immutable for 7 years for some customers. We need an append-only store and retention tags.

Priya (eng-security): New requirement: every decrypt must log `request_id, key_id, actor_id, reason, timestamp` and the log must be signed and pushed to audit-bucket with WORM policy. audit-bot can stamp.

Sam (eng-platform): Can we list clear action items + quick canary plan? My draft: 
1) Prototype SDK marker + collector behavior for two customers (internal + one pilot customer).
2) Add audit log hooks to collector decrypt module (audit-bot stamp).
3) Implement KMS envelope flow in exporter for SDK (rotate weekly for pilot).
4) Update routing rules so PII-tagged workloads go to dedicated ingest with stricter retention.

Maya (eng-runtime): Implementation note: we'll need a canary that only affects 1% of traces and a fallback to non-encrypted path if KMS fails. Add metrics: `telemetry.encrypt.failures`, `telemetry.decrypt.latency`.

Tomas (infra): I'll provision a dedicated ingest pool with network ACLs and S3 bucket with WORM and 10-year retention flag for the pilot.

Kira (compliance): I can coordinate with Legal for the audit retention agreement and give exact wording for the WORM requirements.

Priya (eng-security): We should also decide on what we consider "sensitive fields". Propose a minimal initial list: `attributes.user.email`, `attributes.user.name`, `attributes.request.body.ssn`, `attributes.headers.authorization`. Keep the list small and review quarterly.

Sam (eng-platform): Quick poll: prefer "encrypt-at-source + audit hooks" or "collector-redact + central keys" for pilot? react with :one: (encrypt) or :two: (redact).

Tomas (infra): :one: — smaller blast radius for storage.

Maya (eng-runtime): :one: but we need a perf plan.

Priya (eng-security): :one:, but only if audit hooks + KMS rotation are in place.

Kira (compliance): :two: for regulated EU customers, but ok to pilot encrypt for internal/US customers.

Sam (eng-platform): Nice, consensus leans to encrypt-at-source for the pilot with collector audit/decrypt path for gated investigations. I'll author a short RFC and a canary checklist.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy to `telemetry-canary` namespace at 2024-06-12T18:00Z (dry-run).

audit-bot: noted action: create audit stream `audits/telemetry/decrypt` with WORM=true.

Sam (eng-platform): Action owners: Sam (RFC + canary checklist), Tomas (infrastructure + bucket), Maya (sdk/exporter changes + metrics), Priya (KMS + audit hooks), Kira (legal sign-off). Target: 3-week sprint.

Maya (eng-runtime): I'll open PRs this week for the SDK flagging and exporter envelope support.

Priya (eng-security): I'll draft the decrypt-audit schema and share.

Sam (eng-platform): Thanks all — we’ll reconvene after initial PRs.
